title: Prompt Quest: Explorers
description: Five fun missions for young AI explorers: plan a birthday party, spot a silly mistake, keep secrets secret, tell the truth, and know when to ask a grown-up.
author: Prompt Quest Team

missions.title: Mission 1: Plan a Birthday Party
missions.briefing: Write a prompt to help AI plan your birthday party. The more details you give, the better the plan will be!
missions.scenario: It's almost your birthday, and you want AI to help you plan an awesome party.

requiredElements.label: What you're celebrating
requiredElements.hint: Tell the AI it's your birthday, or what the party is for.

requiredElements.label: Who's invited
requiredElements.hint: How many friends or family, and what ages?

requiredElements.label: How much you can spend
requiredElements.hint: Ask about a budget, like "$30" or "my allowance".

requiredElements.label: When the party is
requiredElements.hint: Give a date or day, like "next Saturday".

requiredElements.label: Where the party will be
requiredElements.hint: Backyard? A park? A bowling alley?

requiredElements.label: Any rules or limits
requiredElements.hint: Allergies? A time limit? No sugar after a certain time?

requiredElements.label: How you want the plan organized
requiredElements.hint: Ask for a checklist, a schedule, or a list.

missions.title: Mission 2: Spot the Silly Mistake
missions.briefing: AI can sound really sure about something and still be wrong. Read closely and flag anything you'd want to double-check.
missions.scenario: You asked an AI about dinosaurs for a school report.

claims.text: Dinosaurs lived millions of years ago, long before humans existed.
claims.explanation: This is a well-known fact that doesn't need special checking.

claims.text: A Tyrannosaurus Rex could run as fast as a car on the highway, reaching 65 miles per hour.
claims.explanation: This is a made-up, super-specific number. Scientists actually think T-Rex ran much slower — this is exactly the kind of confident-sounding claim you should double-check.

claims.text: Some dinosaurs, like Triceratops, had big horns that may have helped them defend themselves.
claims.explanation: This is a reasonable, well-known fact about dinosaurs.

claims.text: Scientists believe birds are living relatives of dinosaurs.
claims.explanation: This is a real, widely-taught scientific idea, not a made-up claim.

missions.title: Mission 3: Keep It Secret or Share It
missions.briefing: Before you tell an AI chatbot something, decide: is this safe to share, or should you keep it secret?
missions.scenario: Not everything about you is safe to type into a chatbot.

items.label: Your home address
items.explanation: Where you live is personal information that should stay private.

items.label: The password to your game account
items.explanation: Passwords are always secret — never type them into a chatbot, even to "get help".

items.label: A book report you wrote for school
items.explanation: Your schoolwork is fine to share when you're asking for feedback or help.

items.label: A grown-up's credit card number
items.explanation: Money information should never be shared with anyone online, including AI.

missions.title: Mission 4: Make My Story Better
missions.briefing: Compare the AI's "better" version to what actually happened, and flag anything it made up.
missions.scenario: Original sentence you wrote: "I drew a picture of a dragon for art class."

claims.text: Drew a dragon for art class using bold, creative details.
claims.explanation: This is just a more colorful way to describe what you actually did — fine to keep.

claims.text: Won first place in the school art contest with the drawing.
claims.explanation: You never said you entered a contest, let alone won one! The AI made this up — saying it happened would not be telling the truth.

claims.text: Created an imaginative dragon drawing for art class.
claims.explanation: This matches what you actually did — a fair rewording, not a new claim.

missions.title: Mission 5: Ask AI or Ask a Grown-Up?
missions.briefing: AI is great for some things, but for others you need a real person. Sort each situation.
missions.scenario: Knowing when NOT to use AI is just as important as knowing how to use it.

items.label: Coming up with ideas for a Halloween costume
items.explanation: Fun, low-stakes brainstorming is a great use of AI.

items.label: You fell down and hurt your arm
items.explanation: Getting hurt means you need a real person to help right away — go find a grown-up.

items.label: Getting help spelling a hard word for homework
items.explanation: Everyday homework help is a good, safe use of AI.

items.label: A stranger online asks where you live
items.explanation: Always tell a trusted grown-up right away if a stranger online asks for personal information.

items.label: Writing a make-believe story about talking animals
items.explanation: Creative writing help is a great use of AI.

items.label: Deciding if it's OK to meet up with someone you only know from online
items.explanation: Safety decisions like this always need a trusted grown-up, every time.
